assessment: Blind text-handoff review against the supplied identity board and brief; no new-content rendering was produced or judged.
ranking_confidence: Moderate. B and A are close; C has several more consequential construction and scope mismatches. This is not a claim about rendered quality or method superiority.
shared_findings: All three identify the source-specific world: flush modular geometry, stepped display lettering, open white or blue reading fields, two anatomically distinct flowers, and unequal trim-connected assemblies. None relies only on generic Memphis labels.

All distinguish the two reading grounds, warm/cool graphic roles and black's limited ornamental role; all avoid copying event copy and exact instance coordinates. Local motif dimensions are useful construction instructions, not inherently a fixed-layout problem.

All acknowledge unknown authorship and original fonts and name substitute materials. Font availability, coverage and licensing were not independently inspected in this restricted review. None demonstrates that its substitute CJK lettering will match the source.

strengths: Very faithful inventory: broad rimmed half-discs, corner-centred arcs, opposite-rounded red block, both flowers, boundary-circle overlap, sprout, cap, stripes and the small satellites. It distinguishes the pale lemon from the golden yellow and keeps the golden flower's pale centre soft and lobed.

Good compositional invariants: connected low skyline, unequal side rises, substantial quiet ground, minority detached accents and blue planes merging into blue fields. Format changes include the materially different large upper panel on narrow strips and the side stack on information cards.

Preserves recomposition freedom especially well. It makes no fixed tile order, mandatory title position or universal image/text ratio, and clearly separates the board surround and object hardware from the identity.
missing_or_contradictory_decisions: Leaves the maker to choose the principal module's scale relative to the object and the title/body/companion scale ratios. 'Large joined geometry' and 'assertive but compact title' do not fully constrain the relative mass that the source repeats.

The arc recipe specifies count and consistent spacing but not how widely the tracks spread through a tile. The red flower lacks a centre-to-flower or dot-to-flower ratio; the golden flower's nested lobe sizes are also largely optical choices.

It flags the CJK fallback problem and suggests custom stepped outlines, but supplies no repeatable finishing unit. A maker may retain the right layout while producing less identifying display texture.
A.practical_significance: A strong, source-faithful handoff with low overconstraint. A fresh maker must supply more proportional judgment than with B, so motif anatomy and overall scale may vary more.

strengths: Most executable identifying construction: the opposing half-discs have a shared seam, explicit outside-edge centres and broad rims; the corner arcs have radii and a broad pitch; both flowers specify lobe/dot/centre relationships; the sprout specifies a common root. These are useful internal relationships rather than copied page coordinates.

Connects scale and silhouette to format without imposing one master page: broad modules start around one fifth of height, narrow strips use enlarged full-width geometry, and portraits may use a transverse band, corner or upper assembly. Explicitly avoids making every portrait a miniature bottom border.

Strong type and colour roles, including the pale-yellow versus golden distinction, flat overlap colours, stacked versus adjacent script pairing and a consistent proposed CJK step unit. Estimated measurements are disclosed as reconstruction guidance.
missing_or_contradictory_decisions: The stacked Latin cap-height range of 0.5–0.65 of the CJK ink height is somewhat large for several source tickets and small portrait pieces, where the Latin companion is closer to roughly two fifths. Applying the upper bound throughout would weaken the source's hierarchy.
'Repeat three' orange triangles turns one observed count into a recipe. The shared baseline, orientation and short ordered run matter more than preserving three with new content.

The golden flower's 'equal-arm cross' could become an overly rectilinear plus unless its soft central contour is retained. Its exact lobe formula and the CJK step size are useful inferred constructions, not verified original geometry.
B.practical_significance: The best starting file for a maker with no reference image, by a narrow margin over A. Its specific motif recipes and format-dependent scale guidance reduce the largest redraw ambiguities. The numerical values still require optical judgment.

strengths: Captures the central joined-edge/open-field grammar and most distinctive motifs. The six-dot rosette and four-lobed nested golden flower remain clearly different; overlap is correctly represented with explicit flat colours.

Useful hierarchy and handling guidance: derives type from the reading zone, distinguishes stacked and adjacent bilingual blocks, gives narrow strips an enlarged top panel, and separates functional information from ornament. The stacked Latin/CJK size range is plausible for the small pieces.
States evidence limits and allows new line breaks, reduced ornament, alternate edges and blue/white arrangements. The file stays content-free.
missing_or_contradictory_decisions: The quarter-arc recipe makes gaps similar to track width. The visible source uses thin tracks with substantially broader gaps across a large part of the tile. This would redraw a conspicuously different, tightly packed rainbow-like unit.

The broad ring thickness of about a quarter module is ambiguous against its merged-cell convention and can be materially heavier than the source's rims. The relationship between a half-disc pair, a basic cell and a merged block needs clarification.

Choosing one dominant motif and allowing a star or diamond as a single floating counterweight overrestricts the evidence: the broad source supports several comparable anchors and simultaneous detached burst, diamond, flower and ring cluster. Those should be compositional options rather than universal limits.

The separate opposite-rounded red block is not actually constructed, despite its prominence on a narrow source strip. The palette also collapses the distinct pale lemon into the golden yellow, reducing an observable light-versus-warm relationship.

The five-to-seven-cells-per-short-side default and linked title/body ranges are useful proposed heuristics, but less securely supported as a common density across all objects. On narrow strips, applying the given type ranges to the half-width module can produce considerably larger type than shown. The general portrait row also underrepresents the source's substantial middle-band option, although the bag row partly restores it.
C.practical_significance: Still likely to produce a recognizable family, but more of its apparent precision needs correction or override. Fixing arc spacing, relaxing single-lead/single-satellite constraints, and clarifying cell scale would improve transfer more than adding further tokens.

overall_practical_significance: The top gap is small: B supplies more redrawable proportions; A preserves observed freedom especially well. C's extra numerical structure does not consistently improve fidelity. All three remain text hypotheses until a fresh maker applies them to new content and the result is compared with the reference.
